implementation_notes: The translator is declared next to the data class: @Serializable with @SerialName("order_id") renames fields, @Serializable(with = ...) or a custom KSerializer object (descriptor, serialize, deserialize over Encoder/Decoder) handles structural and value-level conversion, and the format resolves the serializer through the SerializersModule at runtime. What replaces the classic structure is that compile-time generated serializer plus the Json format configuration - no translator class or registry is hand-written - and an explicit translator remains justified for several wire versions behind one endpoint or when the mapping needs coroutine-bound collaborators such as a repository.
pitfalls: Json { ignoreUnknownKeys = true } is off by default, so a producer adding a field makes decoding throw SerializationException instead of tolerating it - a deliberate but easily forgotten policy switch.
encodeDefaults = false by default drops properties equal to their default value, silently changing the outbound wire shape of an otherwise correct translation.
Custom serializers are looked up per static type in the SerializersModule; a serializer registered for an interface is not used for the concrete class, so the mapping is bypassed without an error.
